comparison: Both strongly support the core findings of neural entrainment and statistical learning in neonates (C3-C5, C37-C39, C42-C43, C56-C57). OpenEval includes additional claims about time course analysis (C44-C46) not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Both evaluations affirm successful learning in both phoneme and voice dimensions with appropriate experimental controls.

OpenEval evaluates Linear Mixed Model time course results (C44-C46) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate statistical methods and lack of significant group differences. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of their overall endorsement of the entrainment results, though they did not explicitly discuss the time course analysis separately.

Perfect claim overlap (C40-C41, C67-C68) but different evaluations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance after multiple comparison correction and between-subjects design limitations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting topographical differences without challenge and praising the combination of neural entrainment and ERP analysis.

Strong agreement on ERP findings (C47-C51). Both evaluations support the cluster-based permutation results showing main effects and lack of interaction. OpenEval explicitly notes the appropriateness of the statistical approach, while peer reviewers accepted findings without objection and found the evidence 'very convincing.'

Both address N400 precursor interpretation (C6, C72, C90). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is plausible but speculative and cannot be definitively established. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing the N400 precursor interpretation without expressing reservations about its speculative nature.

Strong agreement on adult behavioral results (C52-C55, C87). Both evaluations support the findings with appropriate statistical tests. OpenEval notes the marginal significance for voice learning (p=0.050) and acknowledges alternative explanations for developmental differences. Peer reviewers accepted the adult control data as supporting evidence without objection.

Both address main theoretical conclusions about general statistical learning (C60-C62, C89). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for the general learning conclusion but notes the 'common computational principles' claim (C89) is more speculative. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed these conclusions, with all three reviewers explicitly affirming the general-purpose nature of statistical learning.

Both address the claim of no clear advantage for linguistic dimension in neonates (C65-C66). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on lack of significant interactions, appropriately qualified as 'no clear advantage.' Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting that future within-subject studies are needed to definitively establish equal processing.

OpenEval evaluates proto-lexical processing interpretation (C81, C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and requires additional validation. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this theoretical framing as part of their overall positive assessment, with Reviewer 3 specifically praising the theoretical framework adjustments.

Perfect claim overlap on methodological details (C29-C31, C35-C36, C91-C102). Both strongly support the experimental design and methods. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and validated preprocessing pipeline while acknowledging sample size limitations for interaction effects. Peer reviewers praised the 'state-of-the-art' approach, 'clever manipulation,' and 'robust design.'

Both address background literature and theoretical context (C1-C2, C8-C27). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting accurate summarization with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted all background claims through their overall positive assessments, with no challenges to the theoretical framing or literature review.

OpenEval evaluates the primary hypothesis (C28) as SUPPORTED based on experimental results. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this hypothesis statement but implicitly accepted it through their endorsement of the overall study design and findings.

OpenEval evaluates the neural entrainment methodology rationale (C32-C34) as SUPPORTED, noting well-established methods. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this methodological approach through their praise of the 'well-established paradigm' and 'state-of-the-art EEG analysis.'

OpenEval evaluates hemispheric specialization literature citations (C69-C70) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide appropriate context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims but accepted them as part of the overall theoretical framework.

OpenEval evaluates N400 and proto-lexical processing literature (C73-C80, C82-C85) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate citations providing theoretical foundation. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this literature review through their endorsement of the N400 precursor interpretation and overall theoretical framework.

OpenEval evaluates the general statistical learning conclusion (C7) as SUPPORTED and the mechanistic hypothesis (C64) as more speculative. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed the general learning conclusion (C7) as central to the paper's contribution, with explicit affirmation from all reviewers.

Both address broader implications (C64, C66). OpenEval notes C64 is speculative and not directly tested. Peer reviewers endorsed the broader implications about general-purpose learning mechanisms, viewing the findings as 'highly relevant for researchers working in several domains.'

Minor overlap on C71 (posterior negativity for phoneme regularities). OpenEval includes this in broader ERP analysis evaluation (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers include it in their endorsement of the N400 precursor interpretation (SUPPORTED).
